title: dedicated-gpu-pool-autoscale-warmup-debug-breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:
- Breadcrumbs for the Dedicated GPU pool autoscale/warmup incident that caused capacity thrash on 2024-11-29 afternoon ramp. Notes for follow-ups and oncall handover.

High-level problem statement:
- Customer workloads experienced high request latency + 503s during a regional traffic ramp.
- Autoscaler oscillated between scaling up and down (thrash). Many new nodes came up but pods failed ready checks or took long to warm up, making autoscaler continue to add nodes.
- Root cause not fully confirmed; hypothesis list below (warmup time too long, KV cache cold misses, image pull or init container delays, scheduler binpack oscillation).

Timeline (rough):
- 2024-11-29 14:02 UTC: first error spike reported by alerting (p50 latency > 700ms, p95 > 2s).
- 14:05: SRE noticed surge in Pending pods in pool dedicated-gpu-a.
- 14:07: Autoscaler scale-up triggered +6 nodes (policy: target-util 60%).
- 14:10: New nodes register, but readiness probe failures seen for many pods. Pod Start -> Ready delays 40-120s.
- 14:18: Autoscaler sees util still low (because pods not Ready), scales up another +4 nodes.
- 14:30: Some pods eventually Ready but with cold KV cache misses causing additional latency.
- 15:00: Manual intervention: temporarily raise min-capacity for pool and disable aggressive downscale policy.
- 15:20: traffic stabilizes; follow-up meeting scheduled.

Commands tried (local oncall, k8s namespace = dedicated-gpu-a):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --label-columns=pool,instance-type | grep dedicated-gpu-a
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-gpu-a --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n dedicated-gpu-a
- kubectl logs <pod> -n dedicated-gpu-a -c runtime --since=30m
- rictl autoscale status --pool dedicated-gpu-a --window 15m
- rictl pool describe dedicated-gpu-a --show-init-stats
- prometheus query: rate(serving_requests_total[1m]) by (pool)
- grafana dashboard: Dedicated Pools -> warmup latency heatmap (time series).

Key log snippets observed (copied raw):
- "2024-11-29T14:09:42Z ERROR runtime: readiness probe failed: timeout waiting for model init: kv-cache cold, loads exceeded"
- "pod/<name> Warning FailedScheduling 0/12 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 9 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate"
- "eviction manager: pods are being evicted to reclaim resources"
- "docker: image pull failed: registry rate limit?" (only on 2 nodes)

Metrics / Observations:
- Median model init (first request) = 38s (baseline expected ~8-12s).
- KV cache miss rate ~ 78% on new nodes during first 5 minutes.
- GPU utilization across pool averaged 20% during ramp (autoscaler expected to see >60% to avoid scale-down).
- Pod churn high: many pods created then evicted due to transient resource pressure.
- Node boot time (kubelet ready) median = 86s (some up to 180s).

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Warmup sequence too long: model load + cache priming + init containers -> Ready takes >1min. Autoscaler treats Pending as unscheduled capacity demand and keeps adding nodes. Need to add 'warmup' window policy.
2) Autoscaler lacks better hook for "pod warming" — it scales on Scheduled/Pending counts not on Ready or actual serving throughput.
3) Image pull / registry delays + init containers (fs setup, nvidia drivers) add variability. For autoscale, variance creates feedback oscillation.
4) Scheduler bin-packing and taints/tolerations causing misplacement -> repeated evictions.
5) Resource requests/limits misconfigured for some model variants leading to OOMKill/eviction cascades.

Commands / experiments to reproduce (notes):
- Locally simulate traffic ramp using loadgen: ./loadgen --pool dedicated-gpu-a --rps 200 --duration 10m and watch autoscaler decisions.
- Manually cordon a node to force binpack and observe evictions.
- Deploy a canary with forced warmup probe (preload KV cache in init) and compare Ready times.
- Adjust rictl autoscale config: set minWarmupSeconds=120 and see impact in a synthetic test.

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
- Increased pool.min_replicas from 2 -> 6 to cover expected spike window.
- Set autoscaler.downscale_delay to 10m (was 2m) to avoid rapid contraction.
- Disabled aggressive preemption on one subset of nodes.
- Notified oncall SRE to watch registry quotas (possible image pull spikes).

Open action items (for follow-up triage):
- [ ] Run controlled synthetic ramp test with minWarmupSeconds enabled and collect metrics (owner: Asha).
- [ ] Add a warmup metric to autoscaler (count of pods Ready with primed KV cache) and use as signal (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- [ ] Investigate whether we can pre-pull images + layer cache for new nodes as part of node bootstrap (owner: infra).
- [ ] Review resource requests for top N model variants that show frequent OOM/evict (owner: Riley).
- [ ] Add a Postmortem draft linking metrics/graphs and timeline (owner: Jordan).

Notes for postmortem draft (things to include):
- Attach prometheus graphs: p95 latency, pod start->ready histogram, node boot times, KV cache miss rate.
- Include autoscaler config snapshot at incident (rictl dump autoscaler --pool).
- Repro steps and outcomes from loadgen experiments.
- Proposed config changes with risk assessment: minWarmupSeconds, scale-up step limit, use Ready-based scale signal.

Random scratch/thoughts:
- Could be worth caching common embeddings/model weights in a lightweight sidecar that shares a local volume so new pods can warm faster.
- Consider a "warm pool" of pre-initialized standby pods (keeps KV cache hot) vs. reserve nodes. Cost vs latency tradeoff.
- Need better telemetry for init-container phases (separate metrics per phase: image-pull, init, model-load, first-inference).

Links / refs used during debugging:
- https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3245
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (investigating init concurrency)
- Confluence: /spaces/SERV/pages/1954/dedicated-gpu-warmup-guidelines
- Slack: #dedicated-autoscale thread ts:170128DEADBEEF (approx)

If handing off to next oncall: copy this doc, check the rictl autoscale status, don't revert downscale_delay until warmup experiments are done. Keep min_replicas elevated during business hours for a few days if traffic remains spiky.

-- Jordan
